conditions: This approval depends on the separate bounded service-order reviews approving the four global control hashes: documentary_instructions_sha256, expanded_order_sha256, navigation_sha256 and source_order_sha256. The dossier does not give the new values. Each of the 224 rebound receipts must carry exactly the hash those reviews approved. If any value differs from the reviewed control, the rebinding approval is void for that receipt.

It also depends on source closure, including the role label in rh_minchah_half_kaddish.xml. The label is encoded as 'חזן'. No human adjudication from 473 to 489 covers it. The one independent image review (markup-closure-review.json) read it only as 'ח[ז?]ן' and declined to certify it.

markup_verification.musaf_kohanim_dreams.xml: Plain prose in one div/p with one divineName. It has no milestones, quotations or instructions, so there is no scope to get wrong. 'אֲנִי שֶׁלָּךְ וַחֲלוֹמוֹתַי שֶׁלָּךְ' matches adjudication 480.
markup_verification.musaf_repetition_sim_shalom.xml: The pb n=148 opens the first p and matches div/@facs n315. The three prayer-parts (sim_shalom, besefer, proofs) each open with a corresp milestone and close with an explicit terminator inside their own p. The sim_shalom and besefer segs carry @source and close before their terminators. Prov 9:11 and Deut 4:4 are each a seg type=quotation holding a quote-context chapter/verse pair, keyed …/proofs/quotation/{book}/{ch}[/{v}]. Each verse URN is a child of its chapter URN, and @n keeps the canonical values 9/11 and 4/4. Both quoted texts are whole verses, so nothing partial is presented as a canonical whole. Inside each seg the verse terminator comes before the chapter terminator, and both come before the seg closes. The trailing ':' sits outside the seg and inside the proofs prayer-part. The connective words וְנֶאֱמַר and כַּכָּתוּב sit outside the quotations. 'לָּֽנוּ' matches 475.
markup_verification.rh_minchah_ashrei.xml: Ps 84:5 and 144:15 are quotation segs. Each holds its own bounded chapter/verse context, both scopes close inside the seg, and the ':' falls outside. Ps 145 follows the 'milestone before semantic span' pattern. One chapter context milestone is followed by 21 verse milestones, each placed before its own per-verse @source seg, with @n 1–21. After verse 21 come an explicit verse terminator and an explicit chapter terminator. Then Ps 115:18 opens its own chapter/verse context, which is also explicitly closed. All context URNs are children of …/minchah/ashrei, so no canonical bible URN is duplicated. 'סֶּֽלָה', 'לּוֹ' and the meteg on the second lamed of 'יְהַלְלֽוּךָ' match 478 and 483.
markup_verification.rh_minchah_haazinu_levi.xml: I read the full file. The chapter context is …/aliyah/2/quotation/deuteronomy/32, and verses 4, 5 and 6 are its children. Verse 6 has one milestone and two adjacent @source fragments. A shared @source is provenance, not a duplicated corresp, which agrees with the earlier closure review. The enlarged He is <tei:c rend="large">ה</tei:c> followed by patah, in its own seg, matching 481 ('הַ לְיהֹוָה', pashta on יהֹוָה֙ inside divineName). The footnote star is encoded as anchor xml:id=haazinu_large_he just before the enlarged letter. The standOff note type=commentary target=#haazinu_large_he resolves to that anchor. The verse and chapter terminators close the module.
markup_verification.rh_minchah_haazinu_yisrael.xml: The chapter context is …/aliyah/3/quotation/deuteronomy/32, with verses 7–12 as children, each with a per-verse @source seg. Both scopes are explicitly closed. Together with the Levi file (4–6), this gives the standard aliyah split. 'יְסֹֽבְבֶ֙נְהוּ֙' has meteg on the samekh and pashta on both the second bet and the shuruq, matching 482.
markup_verification.rh_minchah_half_kaddish.xml: The role label is a tei:note with corresp urn:x-opensiddur:instruction:role/reader. It comes before the first prayer-part milestone, so it is outside every liturgical scope and the instruction is properly separated. Prayer-parts 1, 2 and 3 each open with a corresp milestone and close with an explicit terminator. 'כִרְעוּתֵהּ' has no kaf dagesh, matching 476.

rebinding_assessment: The dossier states that all 224 old receipts were current before the change. It states that units and source_fidelity are unchanged for all 224. The only changed-field group is the four global control hashes, with count 224, and no other field group appears. That means variants, corrections and the literal/encoding evidence fields are retained unchanged. old_literal_units_sha256 equals same_new_prefix_sha256 (60bbab18…3049), covering 465 units and 837 witnesses. The counts agree: 289 − 224 = 65 new payloads, matching 65 new witnesses in 42 new units, with nothing added to the old units. Rebinding only the four control hashes to reviewed controls, while keeping the old literal evidence, is the right method. It does not require rereading the 837 witnesses, and none is claimed.
limitations: I saw the rebinding evidence only as dossier summary assertions: booleans, field-group counts and two prefix hashes. I did not see the raw old or new receipts, I did not recompute any hash, and I did not check the hashes of the 6 changed files against disk. Approval rests on those assertions being accurate.

The dossier does not say whether the new receipts record which service-order review approved each new control hash. If the binding must be auditable from the receipt itself, a review identifier or reference should be added. I did not treat its absence as blocking, because the bindings are by value.
I read the 6 bodies from bounded-bindings-xml.json and the full file only for rh_minchah_haazinu_levi.xml, to check the footnote. I did not check the headers or standOff of the other five files.

I could not assess alignment against the English counterparts because they were not supplied. In particular, I could not confirm that the EN sim_shalom file uses the same prayer-part and quote-context URNs as the Hebrew one (sim_shalom, besefer, proofs, and …/proofs/quotation/proverbs/9/11, …/deuteronomy/4/4). The earlier review placed an EN-only …/shalom/after_besefer/chatimah unit in that file, and I could not verify how it aligns with the HE structure. I also could not confirm whether the Minchah, Ashrei and Haazinu modules are HE-only or have EN partners with matching URN sets.

Adjudications 473, 474, 477, 479 and 484–489 concern files that are not among the 6 changed bodies. I did not verify that those unchanged files already match the adjudicated readings. That belongs to source closure.
musaf_kohanim_dreams.xml reuses the canonical identity siddur:regalim/musaf/text/dream. I was not given the registry or mapping rows needed to confirm it is mapped only once in this project.

Minor points that do not block approval. The patah of the enlarged He sits outside tei:c. That is valid, but some renderers may split the combining mark at the styling boundary, so moving it inside tei:c (a character cluster) would be more robust. The half-Kaddish label is type=description, while the English rubrics elsewhere are type=instruction. 'ייָ' in Deut 4:4 differs from 'יְיָ' elsewhere in the file, which is a source reading I leave to source review.

I did not certify any source reading or pointing, the footnote text 'ה׳ רבתי, והוא מלה לעצמה.', or the role-label text. I deferred these to the human and independent image reviews. This is not full-batch or export acceptance.
